definitions.explanation: The amount or proportion of sugar contained in food or drink. Also used loosely to refer to sugar or sweets in general, especially when talking about dietary intake.

examples.japanese: {糖分|とうぶん}を{控|ひか}えている。
この{飲|の}み{物|もの}は{糖分|とうぶん}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: This drink has a lot of sugar.

examples.japanese: {疲|つか}れた{時|とき}は{糖分|とうぶん}を{取|と}ると{頭|あたま}がすっきりする。
examples.english: When you're tired, taking in some sugar clears your head.

notes:
USAGE:
{糖分|とうぶん} is commonly used in health and dietary contexts. It refers to sugar in general terms rather than specific types of sugar.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {糖分|とうぶん}を{控|ひか}える (to cut back on sugar)
- {糖分|とうぶん}を{取|と}る (to consume sugar)
- {糖分|とうぶん}が{多|おお}い / {少|すく}ない (high/low in sugar)
- {糖分|とうぶん}{補給|ほきゅう} (sugar intake, replenishing sugar)
